correctness.rationale: Under a silent block history the bias-corrected first moment is exactly \(c_1g\), while Adam-mini's scalar second moment is \(c_2^2\lVert g\rVert_2^2/d\). This gives the displayed update formula. The coordinatewise ratio is bounded by \(\sqrt d\) using \(|g_j|\le\lVert g\rVert_2\), with one-sparse large-amplitude impulses proving sharpness. The \(B\)-block minimax frontier then follows from \(\max_b d_b\ge\lceil N/B\rceil\), and balanced integer block sizes attain equality. The embedded verifier replays these formulas.

value.rationale: Reducing \(N\) coordinatewise learning-rate states to a much smaller number of block states is Adam-mini's defining memory-saving mechanism, and the source explicitly reports that partition choice can control stability. The theorem identifies an unavoidable robustness cost of that compression: with only \(B\) equal-weight block states, even the best partition permits a sparse-coordinate response larger than coordinatewise Adam by \(\sqrt{\lceil N/B\rceil}\). This is a natural, exact memory-versus-update-safety frontier that can inform block-size choices and motivates why sparse or dormant structures deserve special handling.
